cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to Timothy, the man he calls his beloved child (2 Timothy 1:2). He's just finished reminding Timothy what it means to endure for Jesus (2 Timothy 2:1-13). Now Paul says: remind the believers of these things, and charge them before God to steer clear of one kind of fight.

cards.question: Paul wants the believers charged before God to avoid one kind of fight. Which one?
Paul says quarreling over words at least helps the people listening grow sharper.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to Timothy himself: make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman. Not approved by the neighbors, friend, approved to GOD, and that's the only five-star review that counts.

cards.question: Every good workman has something he has to handle with care. What does Paul want Timothy to handle accurately?

cards.text: But Timothy has to avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which Paul says will only lead to more ungodliness. It's the snooze button all over again, friend. One little tap, and somehow you're late for EVERYTHING.

cards.question: Paul compares the talk of men like that to gangrene. He says that talk will ___.

cards.text: And Paul doesn't do the vague 'some people are saying' thing. He names two men who have deviated from the truth: Hymenaeus and Philetus.

cards.question: Hymenaeus and Philetus are saying that the resurrection has already occurred.
What is the teaching of Hymenaeus and Philetus doing to some believers?

answers.text: Pulling them back to the law

cards.text: Sounds grim, but nevertheless, Paul says, God's firm foundation stands, bearing a seal with two sayings on it. Chatter can spread all it wants, friend, that foundation isn't going ANYWHERE.

cards.question: Some believers' faith is being shaken, but God's firm foundation stands. What does the first saying on its seal say?

answers.text: The Lord knows those who are His
Every teacher must be tested first
Hold fast to the old traditions

cards.question: The second saying on the seal: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from ___.

cards.text: Now Paul paints a picture of a large house. It has vessels of gold and silver, but also vessels of wood and clay.

cards.question: In Paul's picture, every vessel in the large house is meant for honorable use.

cards.text: Then Paul tells how a person ends up a vessel for honor. And friend, NOBODY ever mistook this cookie stamper for fine china, so I'm listening close.

cards.question: According to Paul, what makes someone a vessel for honor?

answers.text: Cleansing himself of what is unfit
Being made of gold or silver

cards.question: Paul says a vessel for honor is useful to the Master and prepared for every good work.

cards.text: Then Paul gets personal: flee from youthful passions. Not stroll away, not back away slowly, FLEE, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace.

cards.question: Paul doesn't want Timothy chasing righteousness, faith, love, and peace alone. Who should he pursue them together with?

answers.text: Others who call on the Lord from a pure heart
Others who have suffered hardship for the Lord
Others who have studied the Scriptures since childhood

cards.text: And all that foolish, ignorant speculation? Reject it, Paul says, because Timothy already knows what it leads to.

cards.question: Paul says foolish and ignorant speculation breeds ___.

cards.text: So what should a servant of the Lord look like? Paul runs down the list, and I'm reading it like a job posting I REALLY want.

cards.question: Paul says a servant of the Lord must be quarrelsome when the truth is on the line.
Which of these is on Paul's list of what a servant of the Lord must be?

cards.text: But what about the people who oppose him? Paul says to reprove them, and HOW he does it matters.

cards.question: A servant of the Lord must ___ reprove those who oppose him.
Why reprove them gently? What does Paul hope God may grant the people who oppose a servant of the Lord?

cards.text: If God grants that, Paul says, they will come to their senses.

cards.question: When the people who oppose a servant of the Lord come to their senses, what will they escape?

cards.text: Right now, Paul says, the devil has taken them captive to his will. Friend, I spent years stuck in the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you, stuck is NO way to live.

findings.problem: Verse 14's actual consequence is never told. Marking this statement False only establishes that quarreling over words does not sharpen listeners; no card says that it leads the listeners to ruin, an important detail of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The phrase "men like that" depends on the preceding story card for its antecedent. The question never identifies the men or their irreverent, empty chatter, so it is not self-contained.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question relies on "the seal" and "the second saying" without identifying the seal on God's firm foundation. That context exists only on earlier cards, which the baker can no longer see.

findings.problem: The treatment of verse 24 covers only not being quarrelsome and being kind to everyone. Being able to teach and being forbearing are never told anywhere, leaving important parts of Paul's description of the Lord's servant missing.

findings.problem: The opening clause "If God grants that" uses the condition from verse 25, while coming to their senses is from verse 26. Citing only verse 26 is narrower than the verses the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
